Cycle and history

Restart with new maxes: for coming back after time off or a change in training. Type your current 1RM for each lift; the TM becomes 90% of it and you go back to week 1 of a new cycle. It asks whether to keep or wipe your history. Start next cycle: back to week 1 with your current TMs; history, accessory weights and weak points are kept (Strength lifts from the library are recalculated from your TM for week 1, as at every new week). Wipe history: erases training history and what was built from it, keeps your TMs, goals, Settings and exercise choices (you can export first). Reset Everything: erases all settings, history, program state, accessories and the recovery copies on this phone; this cannot be undone.

What Changed in 2.4

Five changes. The weights and how they progress, the program, and what goes to Hermes are the same.

  • Weak points are remembered. The answer you give after a lift is kept when the app is closed and reopened. Before, most answers were forgotten on reopening, so the stars in the session's accessory list went away. A lift with no stored answer uses the newest answer saved on one of its sessions. Wipe history and Reset Everything erase them all, as before.
  • One set of names. The session's accessory list, its ? sheet and its swap list now say Strength, Muscle, and Core and joints, the names the Accessories screen uses. So do the low-readiness note, the Recovery volume tips, the new-cycle messages and the Recalibrate sheet. They are Tier 1, 2 and 3 of the 3-Tier system this guide describes.
  • Reset Everything leaves nothing behind. It now also deletes the recovery copies on this phone (the copies the app keeps before an update or an import), so no session or answer from before the reset is left and History no longer offers them. Export a backup first if you might want your data back. Wipe history still keeps them; it now replaces the phone's backup copy at once, as Reset Everything does, so the wiped sessions do not linger in it.
  • A hold ends with its cycle. When you take a swap for a weak point, the app holds that target for the wave. A hold from one cycle no longer applies when the same wave comes round in the next cycle. While a hold is on, the session's accessory list stars what the hold targets, as the Accessories screen does. If you mark a different weak point the recap asks Keep or Switch, and Switch moves the hold to the new one at once.
  • Four notes corrected. The ? sheet of a Strength lift from the library says it follows your training max (it said to add weight at the top of the rep range). The stalled-exercise hint points to Program → Open accessories (it said "the Accessories tab"). When no swap can be offered for a weak point, the recap says so and tells you when your gym setting is the reason (it said the library had no such movement). A Strength lift from the library with no log yet says "Load follows the wave." in its open row on Accessories.

What Changed in 2.3

The Accessories screen is new. The weights and how they progress, the program, and what goes to Hermes are the same.

  • Plan first. Your exercises come first, in three sections: Strength, Muscle, Core and joints. Each shows what it is for, its sets, reps, weight and equipment, and a label: Top pick, Best for your gym or Your pick.
  • Coach suggestion. One card, only when there is a reason, with Swap and Keep. It carries the app's own rules (equipment you switched off, the weak point you marked) and any accessory card Hermes has sent for that lift.
  • Swap sheet. Open an exercise and tap Swap exercise: the same purpose first, then other purposes, then what your gym rules out and what each needs.
  • Your gym. The equipment switches, each with the number of exercises it covers. They are the same switches as Settings → Gym Equipment.
  • Recommended plan (rule change). A new plan takes the best exercise you can do for each purpose. With all equipment on it is the same six as before. The plan you have is kept until you tap Reset to recommended.
  • Weak-point swaps (rule change). A Muscle swap is skipped when it would take out your only exercise for a muscle group.

What Changed in 2.2

Changes to what Home shows. The program, the math and your data are the same.

  • Lift buttons. The four lifts sit on one row with short names: Squat, Bench, Deadlift, Press. Under each name is this week's top weight for that lift, or Done or Skipped once it is.
  • Cycle card. The second line says which week you are in. The wave names are at full strength. The key lists only the marks that are on the map. The next test is ringed in its wave's colour.
  • Next test. The line under the map names the lift you have picked and the weight, for example "Squat: 10 or more at 212.5 lb (75%)".
  • Tap a week on Home's map to open Program on that week.

What Changed in 2.1

Fixes from the November 2026 audit of 2.0. The program, the test-day rule and your data are the same.

  • Test day. The test set asks "Log your test?" and shows the reps and what they do to the training max before anything is logged. A second tap within about half a second of a logged set is ignored.
  • Reopening with a workout open picks it straight up. There is no Resume prompt any more (its Cancel deleted the workout).
  • Offline. After one visit with a signal the app opens with a weak signal or none, as long as the file sw.js is published beside it. The font is inside the app file. Settings, under Storage, shows the state.
  • Deleting a session. Swipe left, tap DELETE, confirm. The training max does not change and the lift stays marked for its week.
  • A skipped check-in is saved as skipped and left out of the averages. The sheet at Start has "Not now".
  • Skip asks first every time and does nothing to a lift already done.
  • RPE on "+" sets and tests is saved only if you set it. The rest-screen rating goes to the set you just logged. No rest starts after the last set.
  • Rounding. A weight exactly half-way between two steps always rounds up (a few rounded down).
  • Plates. When your plates cannot make a weight, the app uses the nearest weight they can make and says so on Home.
  • Units. Switching to kg and back returns every number you left alone exactly. In kg the rounding step is 2.5.
  • Numbers read as they are: 67.5% (not 68%), a 210.25 lb max (not 210.3).
  • Home. The deload and backup cards sit under the readiness block. Cancel workout and End early are also at the top of the set screen.
  • Weekly plan. "Days left" counts seven days from your first session of the program week.

What Changed in 2.0

The program, the rules and your data are the same as before. The screens are new. Where this guide says Today or Dashboard it means the Home tab, and History means the Progress tab.

  • Home opens on your readiness score. Check in for today asks the five questions whenever you like. The answer is kept for the day and used once, for the next session you start. Under it are the cycle map, today's lift, the last five weeks and your estimated maxes.
  • The bar above the tabs shows today's lift and a Start button on every tab. During a session it shows the set you are on, or the rest time left, and takes you back.
  • The cycle map shows all sixteen weeks. Each block is one planned set. A white cap is reps you added over the plan on a "+" set or a test. The stepped line is the top set of each week. On Program, tap a week to see it, and pick one lift to see its weights.
  • In a session the log button stays at the bottom and says what it will log. On the rest screen you can rate the straight set you just did (RPE 6 to 10). It is optional, it is saved with the set, and it changes no weight and no training max. If that week's rest timer is 0 there is no rest screen, so nothing is asked.
  • Warm-up ratings are the words Slow, Solid and Fast. They do what the three faces did.
  • Tools shows one tool at a time. The plate calculator has plus and minus buttons and shortcuts to today's weight, the next test and your goal.

What This App Is

A 16-week powerlifting program tracker that tells you what weight to put on the bar, how many sets and reps, how long to rest, and tracks progress. The program is The Juggernaut Method 2.0 with the 10s and 8s waves inverted (many sets of few reps, 10×5 instead of 5×10) per the JTS inverted article; the 5s and 3s waves follow the book's standard table.

On top of the program, the app checks how you're feeling before workouts, can trim volume when you're beat up, and summarises each session. Rules decide; the coach explains. No coach — the app's own or Hermes — sets weights, training maxes or deloads; anything a coach proposes needs your Apply tap and passes the app's own checks first.

Book, JTS Article or App Rule

Every rule in this guide is tagged with where it comes from, and the coaches use the same tags:

  • Book — The Juggernaut Method 2.0 by Chad Wesley Smith.
  • JTS article — Chad Wesley Smith's articles on jtsstrength.com (the inverted 10s/8s waves come from here).
  • App rule — this app's own policy, not part of the method. Examples: readiness set drops, fire days, guided warmup changes, the missed-standard flag and "Reduce TM 5%", the take-a-week-off advice.

What's New in v14

  1. Book program table. 10s and 8s inverted (JTS article); 5s and 3s back to the book's standard table, including 5s intensification 4×5 and 3s accumulation 7×3 / intensification 5×3, with the book's lead-in sets. Only the standard 16-week mode remains.
  2. "+" sets. The last set of every accumulation and intensification week is a "+" set: hit at least the prescribed reps, then stop 2–3 reps short of failure in accumulation and 1–2 reps short in intensification. It is not a max test (book).
  3. The training max is the stored number. Settings shows and edits the TM; the 1RM beside it is for reference.
  4. The book's 5% rule decides how the TM moves after a test (see How the TM Moves).
  5. Test day: warm-ups never include a single at the test weight, and deload weights use the TM from before the test-day increase (book). Backoff sets after the test are gone.
  6. Weight actually lifted. Tap a set's weight to change it; the app asks why with one tap and keeps both the planned and the lifted weight.
  7. Cycles. "Start next cycle" and "Wipe history and start over" at the bottom of Settings; history is no longer deleted automatically.
  8. Hermes. Sessions can go to your Hermes bridge, which sends back suggestion cards and can power the in-app coach.

Fire Days — When You're Ready for More

App rule. A fire day is the flip-side of fatigue management. Fatigue management drops sets when readiness is low (<15/30). Fire day offers an extra set when readiness is exceptional (23+/30).

How it works: after readiness, if your score is 23+/30 the app asks whether to add one set at the same weight and reps as your last working set. Accept adds it; decline keeps the prescription.

Never on: test days (realization) and deload weeks. Readiness set drops don't run on those days either.

Guided Warmup Feedback

App rule. Before your first working set the app can walk you through a warm-up ramp with plate breakdowns and a one-tap rating per set.

Accumulation and intensification days: about 40%, 60% and 80% of the day's first set. Test days: the book's ramp for that wave (it never includes a single at the test weight).

Ratings: Slow (worse than expected), Solid (as expected), Fast (stronger than expected). Only the last 2 ratings count: two Fast add one step to the working sets and two Slow take off two steps. A step is 5 lb for squat and deadlift and 2.5 lb for bench and press (the same sizes as the training-max steps; in kg mode the same numbers in kg), anything mixed changes nothing. A change made this way is logged as a weight change with the reason "warmup feel".

Never changes test-day or deload weights. Turn it off in Settings → AI & Readiness → "Guided warm-up with a rating after each set."

Training Profile & Individualized MEV/MRV

App rule. The Lift Intelligence card's MEV/MRV targets (Minimum Effective Volume / Maximum Recoverable Volume) adjust to a 5-field profile in Settings.

  • Age bracket: under 25 / 25–34 / 35–44 / 45–54 / 55+. Older lifters recover slower → lower MRV.
  • Years of serious training: beginners handle less volume; seasoned lifters have higher work capacity.
  • Bodyweight: informational for now.
  • PED-assisted: raises the MRV ceiling about 10%.
  • Lifestyle stress (1–5): self-reported. High external stress reduces MRV.

The app combines these into a multiplier clamped between 0.75× and 1.25× of the defaults. The defaults (25–34, 3 years, stress 3, no PEDs) give exactly 1.0×.

Settings — Do This First

Program: units lb, bar weight 45, rounding 2.5. Pick your 1RM Formula (Epley, Brzycki or RPE-based) — it's used for estimates such as the calculator, not for TM changes. "Start next cycle" and "Wipe history and start over" are at the bottom of Settings, under Save All Settings.

Lifts & Maxes: enter your training max (TM) for each lift. The TM is the stored number every prescribed weight comes from; the 1RM shown beside it is TM ÷ 0.9, for reference. Your goals (for example 600 deadlift, 405 bench) live here as well. Barbell Profiles are inside this group too: per-lift bar weight, collar weight, rounding and plate inventory, used for exact plate breakdowns.

Rest Timers: a wave×phase grid. The 8s intensification default is 105 s (JTS article; the book says 115 s). The 5s/3s defaults are the app's own (app rule; no source gives values). "0" = no auto-timer.

AI & Readiness: daily readiness check and RPE logging on/off. An OpenRouter key is optional and only a manual alternative to Hermes — one review never goes to two providers.

Hermes: the bridge address and token (Save & connect), "Send to Hermes" (off pauses sending; packets keep queuing), "Use Hermes for the in-app coach" (disabled, with the reason, until Hermes reports its coach is available) and the status line: Synced, Pending, Paused or Needs attention.

Storage: "Persistent Storage" asks the browser to keep this app's data on the device. Where the browser supports it, "Set auto-backup file" picks a file the app keeps a backup in. A note shows whether offline support is active.

UI & Performance: Performance Mode turns off blur and animations on older phones.

Gym Equipment: six toggles (Barbell, Dumbbells, Cables, Bands, Machines, Pull-up Bar). Swap lists only show what you can do; an exercise that needs equipment you've switched off gets an amber warning instead of disappearing, and the coach card on the Accessories screen offers the best swap you can do. The same switches are on Accessories → Your gym, where each shows how many exercises it covers. Props & Implements are inside this group too: boards, blocks, box, adjustable bench, pins, ab wheel, dip bars, foot anchor, SSB, push-up handles. Switch one off and the exercises that need it drop out of swaps and suggestions. "No prop-assisted exercises" switches them all off at once.

Bodyweight: log today's bodyweight; the group shows your latest weigh-in and your last five. A weigh-in is saved only when you tap Log; finishing a session does not add one. Bodyweight is factored into AI coaching prompts and progression context, and is stored locally only.

Training Profile: five fields that adjust your MEV/MRV targets. See "Training Profile & Individualized MEV/MRV" above.

Coach Actions: the list of deload jumps and TM changes, each with Revert. See "How the TM Moves" and "Coach and Hermes" below.

Estimating Your 1RM

On a fresh start the app asks for your 1RM and sets each TM to 90% of it (book). If you've never tested a max:

Option 1 — use a recent heavy set. If you can bench 185 lb for 5, open the Tools tab, enter 185 and 5, and use the estimate.

Option 2 — be conservative. Use a weight you could do for 3 slow, controlled reps as your 1RM. Starting light is better than starting heavy; the first test day corrects it.

Don't inflate the numbers. Every prescribed weight comes from the TM. Too high and you grind reps, miss rep standards and the progression stops working.

The 16-Week Program

Four 4-week waves — 10s, 8s, 5s, 3s — each with the same weekly rhythm: Accumulation (volume), Intensification (heavier, fewer reps), Realization (test day) and Deload (recovery; never skipped). Percentages are of your TM.

WaveAccumulationIntensificationTest day
10s
JTS article		10×5 @ 60%, 60 s10×3 @ 67.5%, 90 s50%×5, 60%×3, 70%×1, then 75% × AMRAP (standard 10)
8s
JTS article		8×5 @ 65%, 75 s8×3 @ 72.5%, 105 s50%×5, 60%×3, 70%×2, 75%×1, then 80% × AMRAP (standard 8)
5s
Book		6×5 @ 70%, 120 s65%×2, 72.5%×2, then 4×5 @ 77.5%, 150 s50%×5, 60%×3, 70%×2, 75%×1, 80%×1, then 85% × AMRAP (standard 5)
3s
Book		7×3 @ 75%, 180 s70%×1, 77.5%×1, then 5×3 @ 82.5%, 180 s50%×5, 60%×3, 70%×2, 75%×1, 80%×1, 85%×1, then 90% × AMRAP (standard 3)

Deload weeks: 40%, 50% and 60% × 5, worked out from the TM you had before that wave's test-day increase (book).

"+" sets: the last set of every accumulation and intensification week (book). Do at least the prescribed reps, then stop 2–3 reps short of failure (accumulation) or 1–2 short (intensification). It isn't a max test. The 2012 JTS article used straight sets for the inverted waves; the "+" set there is Reese's choice. Each "+" set shows a rep goal from the same week of your last cycle.

The timeline bar shows all 16 weeks — blue glow = current, green = done, faded = upcoming.

Scheduling Your Training Week

You train 4 sessions per week — one lift per session. Each session you pick one of your four lifts (Squat, Bench, Deadlift, OHP), do the main lift, then that lift's accessories. A typical split: Monday Squat · Tuesday Bench · Thursday Deadlift · Friday OHP.

Two habits help: avoid training two days in a row, and separate squat and deadlift by at least two days. The Weekly Plan’s next-up suggestion follows this: after a session today or yesterday it offers a lift for the other half of the body (upper or lower) first, and when every lift left would break one of these it suggests a rest day instead, and you can still pick any lift. A program week means completing all 4 lifts once; when every lift chip is checked, the program moves to the next week. Order within the week doesn't matter.

Dashboard

With no session active, the dashboard shows where you are (cycle, wave, phase), which lifts are done this week (tap a chip to preview), and the workout preview with weight, plates, scheme, rest and percentage. Last Session shows your most recent result for that lift, including the test result on test days.

Cards that can appear: a TM confirmation after a test lifted at a different weight than planned (Apply TM change / Keep TM); Hermes suggestion cards with Apply and Dismiss; the deload banner; goal ETA cards once a lift has 3 tests; and, at the end of a cycle, Start next cycle.

Readiness card: shown under the workout preview once you have a scored check-in and readiness is switched on. It shows your latest score out of 30, the change from the check-in before, your last seven scores, and what that check-in did to its session: working sets dropped, full volume restored by you, an extra set taken or not taken, or no change; on a test day it says readiness did not change the session. For an older check-in whose record does not say, it shows the rule for that score instead (below 8 two working sets are dropped, below 15 one, and at 23 and above an extra set is offered). A score that is not a whole number shows one decimal (7.5/30), wherever the score is shown. It only informs; nothing on it changes your training. Deload-week check-ins are left out, as in the Readiness Trend.

Timeline Bar

The pills at the top show all 16 weeks. Tap any week to preview its weights for every lift; "Back to current" returns. The Program tab shows the same 16 weeks as a grid, with a volume bar and a top-set bar in every week.

Lift Intelligence

Per-lift weekly hard sets against the MEV/MRV targets for that phase (warm-up and ramp sets excluded). Your Tier 1 accessories are the volume lever.

Weekly Plan

Lifts done vs. remaining, days left, a pace badge, and a "Next up" suggestion that respects squat/deadlift spacing.

Daily Workout Flow

Readiness Check

Tap Start Workout and rate Sleep, Motivation, Nutrition, Soreness and Performance 1–5 (a "Same as Last" button fills them from your last session). The app turns them into a 0–30 score. App rule: below 15 drops one working set, below 8 drops two; "Train Full Volume Anyway" overrides. Never on test days or deloads.

Logging Sets

Tap a set row to log it when the reps match the target, or use the hero card's stepper. The hero card shows the weight, a plate diagram with each plate’s weight on it (iron or colour-coded: Settings → Program → Plate drawing), target reps and % of TM.

Changing the Weight

Tap a set's weight to change it. The app asks why with one tap — felt heavy, felt light, plates or equipment, pain, short on time, other — and keeps both the planned and the lifted weight. A change can apply to the rest of the work sets too.

RPE

Optional on "+" sets and the test. RPE 8 = 2 reps left, 9 = 1 left, 10 = nothing left. Nothing is saved unless you set it. It's recorded for review only — RPE never changes main-lift loads.

Rest Timer and Session Timer

The rest sheet counts down and previews the next set's weight and plate changes. Tap the session timer badge to pause/resume; paused time isn't counted.

Mid-Session Check

After 3 working sets: "How's the movement feeling?" — Sluggish / Normal / Dialed In. Stored for the coach.

Test Day (Realization, Week 3 of Each Wave)

Ramp sets first (the book's ramp for that wave, shown with blue "RAMP" pills; never a single at the test weight), then one AMRAP at the test weight: 75% (10s), 80% (8s), 85% (5s) or 90% (3s) of your TM. The rep standard is 10, 8, 5 or 3.

This AMRAP is the only max test in the program. If you enter more than 8 reps over the standard, the app asks you to confirm the number (a check against stepper slips, not a limit).

No readiness set drops, fire days or warmup weight changes on test day. The test result decides the TM (next section).

How the TM Moves

After a test (book):

  • Extra reps = reps − standard, at most 10. Zero or fewer extra reps: the TM is held.
  • Full step = extra × 5 lb (squat, deadlift) or extra × 2.5 lb (bench, OHP). Half step = extra × 2.5 lb (lower body) or extra × 1.25 lb (upper body).
  • The book's 5% rule: projected max = weight × reps × 0.033 + weight. Use the full step if projected ÷ (TM + full step) ≥ 1.05; otherwise the half step if projected ÷ (TM + half step) ≥ 1.05; otherwise no increase. The last step is an app rule: the book stops at the half step. In practice it usually takes 3 reps over the standard to earn a raise (2 on the 8s), and more at lower training maxes.
  • The weight is the one you actually lifted. If it differs from the plan, the increase waits for your OK on the dashboard (Apply TM change / Keep TM). It applies only to the TM it was worked out from: if the TM changes first (a Settings edit, a later test, a cut), the card says so and offers Keep current TM instead.
  • The deload that follows uses the TM from before the increase.

Missed rep standard (app rule — the book has none): the TM is held and the miss is flagged. After 2 misses in a row on one lift, the app offers "Reduce TM 5%" (TM × 0.95). It checks the evidence each time: one cut per new set of misses, and another cut for that lift needs a new test after the last cut. The old TM is kept in Settings → Coach Actions for a one-tap revert, as long as the TM is still the one the cut left (after a later test, a Settings edit or another cut the entry shows "stale", so a newer TM is never overwritten; undo the newest cut first). There's no repeat-wave option.

Estimated 1RM comes only from test days. 10s and 8s tests are marked "lower confidence"; deloads are left out of every trend.

Cycles, Wipe and Reset

Start next cycle (bottom of Settings, or the dashboard when a cycle is complete): back to week 1 with your current TMs carried into the next 10s wave. History is kept and every session keeps its cycle number, so "+" sets and tests compare with the same week of earlier cycles. Accessory weights, progress and weak points are kept. One exception, as at every new week: Tier 1 lifts from the library follow your TM and the wave, so they are recalculated for week 1 (a Tier 1 weight you set by hand lasts until the week turns over, and a new cycle counts as a new week, even when you start it from week 1). Exercises you added yourself and Tier 2 and 3 keep their weights.

Before a new cycle (app suggestion, not from the book): a week off or a light week of general fitness can help clear 16 weeks of fatigue. If you missed rep standards, the app's "Reduce TM 5%" (app rule, above) is the built-in way to restart lighter; you can also edit any TM in Settings.

Restart with new maxes (bottom of Settings): for coming back after weeks off, or when a change in training has moved your maxes up or down. Type your current 1RM for each lift; the TM becomes 90% of it (the book's starting rule) and a lift you leave alone keeps its TM. Then choose: Keep history starts the next cycle at week 1, exactly as "Start next cycle" does, with the new TMs; Wipe history runs "Wipe history and start over" first. Hermes is told about each changed TM the same way as when you edit one in Settings.

Wipe history and start over: asks "Export first?", then erases sessions, accessory logs and progress, weak points, PR records, coach notes and chat, the coach action log, wave summaries and TM-cut blocks. It keeps your TMs (and the 1RM beside them), goals, everything in Settings and your accessory choices, and goes back to week 1, cycle 1. Accessory weights go back to the app's starting weights from your TM, also for a library exercise you renamed; exercises you added go back to the last weight you typed (0 if none). A library exercise renamed in v13.2.2 or earlier can't be matched to the library: the confirmation names it and its weight is kept.

Reset Everything (bottom of Settings, with the cycle buttons) also erases Settings, including the Hermes address and token. Enter them again to pair this phone with Hermes again. It also deletes the recovery copies on this phone, so nothing from before the reset is left: export a backup first if you might want your data back.

Nothing is deleted automatically any more: history is kept however long it gets. Only the smaller backup copy in the browser may be trimmed if storage is full.

Accessories — Continuous Flow

After the main lift, tap "Continue to Accessories →" to log accessories inline.

3-Tier System: Strength (T1: supplemental, 5–8 reps) · Muscle (T2: hypertrophy, 8–15) · Core and joints (T3: core and prehab, 10–20). The screens use the names. This guide also uses the tier numbers.

The Accessories screen (Program → Open accessories) shows your plan first: the exercises for the lift you pick, in three sections named Strength (T1), Muscle (T2) and Core and joints (T3). Each exercise shows what it is for and a label. Top pick is the library's first choice for that purpose. Best for your gym is the best one you can do when the top pick needs equipment you've switched off. Your pick is anything else. Tap an exercise to open it. Swap exercise lists the same purpose first, then other purposes, then what your gym rules out and what each needs. Everything the row had before is still there: reps, Save Log, Apply ↑, Deload, move, duplicate and delete.

Coach suggestion: a card shows above the plan only when there is a reason: an exercise needs equipment you switched off, the weak point you marked has a matching swap, or Hermes has sent an accessory card for that lift (the card Home shows, with the same Apply and Dismiss). Swap applies it. Keep hides it; a weak-point suggestion comes back only if you mark the same weak point again. A dot on a lift's tab means that lift has a suggestion.

Recommended plan: a new plan takes the best exercise you can do for each purpose, two per section, instead of the first two you can do. With all equipment on it is the same six as before. The plan you have is never changed without a tap. Reset to recommended appears when your plan differs; exercises that stay keep their weight and progress, and Undo puts the old plan back.

Double progression: hold the weight, build reps. All sets at the top of the range → green glow → Apply ↑. Deload weeks cut the sets.

Exercises you added remember the last weight you typed for them (Add, Duplicate, an edit under Program → Open accessories, or a swap into a custom slot). Apply ↑, deloads and recalibration don't change that remembered weight; Wipe history goes back to it. An exercise you added also has a Loaded on a barbell switch (off by default): when it is on, Deload lands on a weight you can load with that lift's bar, collars and plates, as it does for the library's barbell exercises.

Tap ? on an exercise for cues, a tutorial link and swap chips. Each inline card also has ⇄ Swap, which lists the legal alternatives for that tier (filtered by equipment and props), with exercises for your weak point at the top. ▲/▼ reorder exercises.

Weak Point Targeting: after a session the app asks "Where did you struggle?" and suggests up to two targeted swaps. A Muscle swap is skipped when it would take out your only exercise for a muscle group. The same suggestion shows on the Accessories screen. Your answer stays with that lift until you give another one, also when the app is closed and reopened: accessories that target it carry a star in the session's list. When you take a suggested swap, the app holds that target for the rest of that wave: the stars follow the hold, and if you then mark a different weak point the recap asks Keep or Switch (Switch moves the hold to the new one). Wipe history and Reset Everything erase your answers.

History Tab

Calendar: a month grid at the top. A day you trained is filled in the colour of its wave (10s yellow, 8s amber, 5s orange, 3s red, deload lavender) and marked with the lift (SQ, BP, DL, OHP). A dashed outline means a session that day was ended early. Today is ringed. Tap a day to see its sessions; the arrows change the month.

Weekly Summary: sessions, sets, tonnage and average readiness against last week. Tonnage is worked out one way everywhere in the app: the sets you performed, leaving out ramp-up and lead-in sets. Total Sets counts the same sets, so it agrees with the Session Log rows. An average readiness that is not a whole number shows one decimal.

Sparklines chart the TM per lift (green) and readiness (amber); volume is in the Weekly volume chart, which has a lift filter. Each session shows its outcome, the test result on test days (reps vs. standard, TM change), a cycle tag, any weight changes with their reason, and whether a coach review is pending.

Lift page: tap a lift's TM card (View details) to see its TM over time with dates, its test days (reps against the standard, TM before and after, test e1RM) and its heaviest sets by rep range (every logged set counts, lead-in singles included). Nothing can be edited there.

Weekly volume: one bar of tonnage per calendar week (Monday to Sunday), coloured by wave. Choose a range and a lift; tap a bar, or use Earlier and Later, for that week's tonnage and session count. A week with no sessions is left empty, and so is a week whose sessions have no counted set (for example a test day ended after one ramp set) or whose counted sets add up to zero; the calendar and the Session Log still show those sessions. Ramp-up and lead-in sets are not counted, as in each session's tonnage line, and sets you did not perform never count.

Wave summaries compare test to test: TM before and after, and reps against the standard.

Session notes can be added on the completion screen. Filter by lift. Swipe left and tap DELETE to delete a session; the app asks first. Deleting does not change a training max, and the lift stays marked for its week. (A deleted session isn't removed on Hermes's side — the bridge has no message for it.) Export makes a JSON backup without your keys or the Hermes token; Import shows a preview before replacing anything, and History → Undo import restores what you had.

Coach and Hermes

After every session the app shows its own rule-based summary at once ("Coach: rules"). With Hermes's coach switched on, Hermes's review replaces it when it's ready — even if you close and reopen the app — labelled "Coach: Hermes · model".

Number check: every number in a coach reply must come from your data. A reply that fails is retried once; if it fails again you keep the rule-based summary. Suggestion cards that fail the check are dropped.

Suggestion cards can propose only: swap an accessory, ±1 accessory set, Reduce TM 5% (only through the evidence check), pull the deload forward, or add a note. Each needs your Apply tap and passes the app's checks; every applied card is in Settings → Coach Actions with a Revert button.

Coach tab: chat through Hermes, or through your own OpenRouter key as a manual alternative. There's no automatic fallback to a paid API.

What goes to Hermes: a packet after every session and a weekly catch-up, over HTTPS with your token. If Hermes can't be reached, packets wait in a queue (at most 500) and go when it's back. With no bridge set up, nothing is sent. A test day ended early before its test is reported to Hermes the same way as a skipped test.

System Philosophy

What Is the Juggernaut Method?

The Juggernaut Method was created by Chad Wesley Smith, founder of Juggernaut Training Systems. It combines wave loading with submaximal training: strength is built by accumulating quality reps at submaximal loads, not by testing your max every week. The method controls how much stress you apply, when you apply it, and when you back off.

What Is the Inverted Version?

The book's 10s wave uses sets of 10 and the 8s wave sets of 8. The inverted 10s and 8s waves from the JTS article flip this: 10 sets of 5 and 8 sets of 5 (then 10×3 and 8×3). Same work, but every rep stays in the quality zone. In this app only the 10s and 8s waves are inverted; the 5s and 3s waves follow the book's standard table.

Why Waves?

Waves move from higher reps to lower reps: the 10s wave builds work capacity, the 8s bridges to strength, the 5s builds strength, the 3s peaks it. Each wave ends with a test that moves the TM.

Why Accumulation → Intensification → Realization → Deload?

Accumulation applies volume at moderate weight. Intensification drops volume and raises the weight. Realization tests what you built with one AMRAP. Deload lets you absorb the training. Stress → adapt → test → recover.

Why a 90% Training Max?

Starting the TM at 90% of your max (book) means every prescribed weight is one you can handle on a bad day. The test-day rule then moves the TM by what you actually showed, and the 5% rule keeps the projected max at least 5% above the new TM.

The 3-Tier Accessory System

Strength (Tier 1: supplemental, 5–8 reps): barbell variations for where your lift breaks down (Pause Squats for the bottom, Close-Grip Bench for lockout). Muscle (Tier 2: hypertrophy, 8–15): build the prime movers and keep push/pull balanced. Core and joints (Tier 3: core and prehab, 10–20): keep you training consistently.

Why Double Progression for Accessories?

Hold the weight and build reps; when every set reaches the top of the range, add the increment and start again. Simple and self-regulating.

How the Defaults Are Selected

Each lift's defaults cover both sides of the lift (bottom position and lockout), balanced push/pull in T2 and prehab in T3. The category next to each exercise says when to use it.

Your Workout: Start to Finish

Step 1 — Check the Dashboard

Settings open from the sliders button in the header. The Today tab shows the cycle, wave, phase and week (e.g. "5S · Intensification · Wk 10/16"), the lift buttons (this week's top weight under each name, or Done once it is), the workout preview with plates, your last session and the Weekly Plan. Lift Intelligence is on the Recovery screen (tap the Recovery tile). Any TM confirmation or Hermes card waits here.

Step 2 — Start Workout

Tap Start Workout and rate readiness. Below 15/30 the app drops a working set (app rule; not on test days or deloads); "Train Full Volume Anyway" overrides. 23+/30 offers a fire-day set (app rule).

Step 3 — Warm Up and Work

If guided warmup is on, rate each warm-up set. Then work through the sets: lead-ins first on 5s/3s intensification days, then the working sets. Tap a row to log it, or tap the weight to change it and pick a reason.

Step 4 — The "+" Set

The last set of an accumulation or intensification day. Do at least the prescribed reps and stop 2–3 short of failure (accumulation) or 1–2 short (intensification); the rep goal from the same week last cycle is shown. Enter the reps you did.

Step 5 — Test Day

On week 3 of a wave: the book's ramp, then one AMRAP at 75/80/85/90% of TM. Enter your reps; the result decides the TM by the book's 5% rule.

Step 6 — Complete Session

The completion screen shows the summary (with the test, the "+" set and the TM change on test days), the coach summary, session difficulty, a notes box and "Where did you struggle?" for accessory targeting.

Step 7 — Accessories

Tap "Continue to Accessories →", log each exercise with the steppers, swap with ⇄ if needed, then "Finish Full Session".

If You Need to Leave Mid-Workout

Close the app at any point; the session is saved. Next time you open it, the workout is picked up where you left it.

Started by mistake? Before any set is logged, Cancel workout (under Complete Session) discards the session: nothing goes to History, the lift stays due this week and that session's readiness check-in is not kept. Once a set is logged the button is End early instead, which saves the sets you did.

Installing as an App (PWA)

iPhone (Safari): Share → "Add to Home Screen." Android (Chrome): menu → "Add to Home Screen" or "Install App."

Your data is stored on the phone (IndexedDB, with a backup copy in the browser). Train from one place — the home-screen app or a Safari tab — because on iPhone the two can keep separate data.

Offline: after one visit with a signal the app keeps a copy of its page and opens from it when the signal is weak or gone. Settings, under Storage, says "Offline copy saved" when it is in place. It needs the file sw.js published beside the app.

Resuming Unfinished Sessions

If you close the app mid-workout, the session is kept. Next time the app opens it picks the workout up where you left off and says which set you are on. Nothing asks, so nothing can be dropped by a wrong tap. To drop a workout on purpose: Undo its sets and use Cancel workout, or use End early to keep the sets you did.

Key Terms

TMTraining Max — the stored number every weight comes from (starts at 90% of 1RM) 1RMOne Rep Max — heaviest you can lift once (shown as TM ÷ 0.9) AMRAPAs Many Reps As Possible — the test-day set + SetLast set of accumulation/intensification: prescribed reps or more, stop 2–3 (or 1–2) short of failure Rep StandardThe test's target: 10, 8, 5 or 3 reps 5% RuleThe book's check that the projected max stays 5% above the new TM RPERate of Perceived Exertion — 1–10, how hard a set felt RIRReps In Reserve — reps left (RPE 8 = 2 RIR) e1RMEstimated 1RM — from test days only TonnageTotal weight moved — sets × reps × weight AccumulationHigh volume week IntensificationHeavier weight, moderate volume RealizationTest day — one AMRAP measures progress DeloadRecovery week — 40/50/60% of the pre-test TM WaveA 4-week block (10s, 8s, 5s, 3s) CycleOne run through all 16 weeks InvertedMany sets × few reps (10×5 not 5×10) — the 10s and 8s waves Double ProgressionHold weight, build reps — ceiling triggers weight increase AutoregulationApp rule: readiness trims volume on hard days Ramp SetWarm-up set before the test-day AMRAP MEVMinimum Effective Volume — fewest weekly sets to make progress MRVMaximum Recoverable Volume — most weekly sets before recovery breaks HermesReese's own bridge on the Mac: archives packets, reviews waves, sends cards PWAProgressive Web App — installable on the home screen Performance ModeDisables blur/animations for faster rendering on older devices

Welcome to Juggernaut 2.4

A 16-week powerlifting tracker built on Chad Wesley Smith's The Juggernaut Method 2.0, with the 10s and 8s waves inverted (many sets × few reps) as in his JTS article. "+" sets that stop short of failure, one test-day AMRAP per wave, double-progression accessories. Three quick steps to get you training.

Step 1 — Enter your 1-rep maxes (honest, not ego)
Step 2 — The app sets each training max to 90% of it
Step 3 — Start your first session. All four lifts are on; switch any off in Settings.

Your 1-Rep Maxes

Enter the heaviest weight you can lift for exactly 1 rep with good form. If you don't know, use a recent heavy set and the calculator tool later. Be conservative — the whole program is built on this being honest.

Ready to Train

You're all set. Each training max (TM) starts at 90% of the 1RM you entered (book), and every prescribed weight comes from it. From now on the TM is the number that moves after each test; you can see and edit it in Settings.

Tip: Tap the ? icon in the header anytime to read the full method guide. It covers all 16 weeks, test days, how the TM moves, accessories and the coach, and marks which rules are the book's and which are the app's.
